'''Hsien Chung''' (or '''Hsien-Chung''' or '''Hsien-chung''') '''Wang''' (王宪钟 ''Wang Xian Zhong''; 18 April 1918 in [[Beijing]] – 25 June 1978 in [[New York City]]) was a Chinese-American mathematician, specializing in [[differential geometry]], [[Lie group]]s, and [[algebraic topology]].

==Biography==
Hsien Chung Wang was part of a family from [[Shandong Province]] that had produced distinguished scholars for several generations, including the archeologist [[Wang Yirong]].<ref name=":0">{{cite journal|url=http://www.encyclopedia.com/doc/1G2-2830905387.html|title=Wang, Hsien Chung|website=|date=2008|publisher=[[Charles Scribner's Sons]]|journal=[[Complete Dictionary of Scientific Biography]]}}</ref>

He studied in [[Tianjin]] at [[Tianjin Nankai High School|Nankai High School]] and in 1936 he matriculated at [[Tsing Hua University]] in [[Beijing]]. Due to the outbreak of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]] in 1937, the university had to be moved to Southwest China. Wang graduated in 1941 and began to study under [[Shing-Shen Chern|Chern]]. He was awarded a master's degree in 1944 and began teaching in a school.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Wang|title=Hsien Chung Wang}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web |author-last1=Rosenberg |author-first1=Alex |author-link1=Alex F. T. W. Rosenberg |author-link3=Wolfgang Heinrich Johannes Fuchs |title=Hsien Chung Wang 1918–1978, Cornell University Faculty Memorial Statement |url=https://ecommons.cornell.edu/bitstream/handle/1813/18102/Wang_Hsien-Chung_1978.pdf |access-date=2023-09-08 |website=ecommons.cornell.edu |author-last2=Rothaus |author-first2=Oscar S. |author-last3=Fuchs |author-first3=Wolfgang H.}}</ref>

However, after one year, he was awarded a [[British Council]] Scholarship to continue his studies in England. He studied first in [[University of Sheffield|Sheffield]] and then at [[University of Manchester|Manchester University]] under [[Max Newman|Newman]], and received a Ph.D. in 1948.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2" /><ref name=":1" />

Returning to China, Wang took a research position at the [[Academia Sinica]], which was soon moved to [[Taiwan]] following the end of the [[Chinese Civil War]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2" />

In 1949 Wang moved to the United States, obtaining a lecturer position at [[Louisiana State University]]. In the subsequent years, he hold a series of temporary positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton|Institute for Advanced Study at Princeton]], the [[Alabama Polytechnic Institute]], the [[University of Washington in Seattle]] and [[Columbia University in New York]].<ref name="MacRef2" /><ref name=":1" />

He obtained his first permanent position in 1957 at [[Northwestern University]]. In 1966 he accepted a professorship at [[Cornell University]], which he hold until his sudden death from leukemia.<ref name="MacRef2" /><ref name=":1" />

== Research and awards ==
While he was a PhD student in Manchester,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1949-03-01 |title=The homology groups of the fibre bundles over a sphere |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/duke-mathematical-journal/volume-16/issue-1/The-homology-groups-of-the-fibre-bundles-over-a-sphere/10.1215/S0012-7094-49-01603-8.full |journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]] |volume=16 |issue=1 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-49-01603-8 |issn=0012-7094|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Wang worked in [[algebraic topology]]. He discovered an [[exact sequence]] (called nowadays the [[Spectral sequence#Wang sequence|Wang sequence]]) involving the [[homology groups]] associated with [[Fiber bundle|fiber bundles]] over spheres.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2" />

At the same time,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1949 |title=Homogeneous Spaces with Non-Vanishing Euler Characteristics |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1969588?origin=crossref |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=925 |doi=10.2307/1969588|url-access=subscription }}</ref> he also solved an open problem arising from the work of [[Heinz Hopf|Hopf]] and [[Hans Samelson|Samelson]]:<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hopf |first=H. |author-link=Heinz Hopf |last2=Samelson |first2=H. |author-link2=Hans Samelson |date=1940 |title=Ein Satz über die Wirkungsräume geschlossener Liescher Gruppen. |trans-title=A theorem on the action spaces of closed Lie groups |url=https://eudml.org/doc/138771 |journal=[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]] |language=de |volume=13 |issn=0010-2571 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20260607154949/https://eudml.org/doc/138771 |archive-date=2026-06-07}}</ref> determine the closed subgroups of maximal [[Rank of a group|rank]] in a [[compact Lie group]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2" /> In 1952<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1952 |title=Two-Point Homogeneous Spaces |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1969427 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=55 |issue=1 |pages=177–191 |doi=10.2307/1969427 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> he showed that any [[Connected space|connected]] [[Compact space|compact]] [[metric space]], such that any two pairs of points separated by the same distance are related by an [[isometry]], is a [[homogeneous space]] of a compact Lie group.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2" />

Since 1956<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1956 |title=Discrete Subgroups of Solvable Lie Groups I |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1969948?origin=crossref |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=64 |issue=1 |pages=1 |doi=10.2307/1969948|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and until the end of his career he worked mostly on [[Discrete group|discrete subgroups]] of [[Lie group|Lie groups]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="MacRef2" />

Among other topics in [[differential geometry]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Boothby |first=William Munger |author-link=William M. Boothby |last2=Chern |first2=Shiing-Shen |author-link2=Shiing-Shen Chern |last3=Wang |first3=Shu Ping |date=1980 |title=The mathematical work of H. C. Wang |url=https://www.math.sinica.edu.tw/bulletin/journals/1543 |journal=Bulletin of the Institute of Mathematics Academia Sinica |volume=8 |issue=2,3 Part 1 |pages=XIII-XXIV |mr=595525 |zbl=0446.01026}}</ref><ref name="MacRef2" /> he worked on [[Complex manifold|complex manifolds]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1954 |title=Complex parallisable manifolds |url=https://www.ams.org/proc/1954-005-05/S0002-9939-1954-0074064-3/ |journal=[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=5 |issue=5 |pages=771–776 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-1954-0074064-3 |issn=1088-6826}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1954 |title=Closed Manifolds with Homogeneous Complex Structure |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2372397?origin=crossref |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=76 |issue=1 |pages=1 |doi=10.2307/2372397|url-access=subscription }}</ref> he described a construction of [[Contact geometry|contact manifolds]] which is now called the [[Boothby-Wang construction]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Boothby |first=W. M. |last2=Wang |first2=H. C. |date=1958 |title=On Contact Manifolds |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1970165 |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=68 |issue=3 |pages=721–734 |doi=10.2307/1970165 |issn=0003-486X|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and he studied [[transformation groups]] of [[N-sphere|n-spheres]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hsien-Chung |date=1960 |title=Compact Transformation Groups of Sn with an (n - 1)-Dimensional Orbit |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2372936 |journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=82 |issue=4 |pages=698–748 |doi=10.2307/2372936 |issn=0002-9327|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Wang was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] in 1958 in Edinburgh.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1958/ICM1958.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 1958 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |year=1960 |editor-last=Todd |editor-first=John Arthur |editor-link=J. A. Todd |location=Cambridge |pages=500-509}}</ref> He was a [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1960|Guggenheim Fellow for the academic year 1960–1961]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hsien Chung Wang |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/hsien-chung-wang |access-date=2026-08-19 |website=[[Guggenheim Fellowships]]}}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Stephen Halperin|J. Stephen Halperin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pi.math.cornell.edu/m/doctorates1970-79|title=Cornell Mathematics Doctorates, 1970-1979|access-date=2023-09-08}}</ref>
